checks: Translate the common shape to centroid zero and absorb the translation into each a_i. Positivity and full dimension give w_i=|K|₍d₎r_i^d. Convexity of K gives λK+μK=(λ+μ)K for positive coefficients. Comparing volumes of the exact fiber Minkowski midpoint sets yields radius midpoints, and comparing their centroids yields a_i midpoints. This also holds for d=1 and for ties among parity maxima.
Root orders give w₀≤w₂, w₅≤w₃ and w₇≤w₄. The radius identity r₆=(r₇+r₄)/2 gives r₆≤r₄, and r₂=2r₄−r₆ gives r₄≤r₂. Positive powers give w₆,w₇≤w₄≤w₂. Hence C≤2w₄≤w₄+w₂≤B+G.

At q₃ and q₂ the own marks give A and G. At q₁ the retained own mark and one midpoint partner give L because w₀≤w₂. At q₄ the pairs q₃,q₅ are opposite, and q₆−q₄=q₄−q₂ and q₇−q₄=2(q₄−q₂). If the cap normal is nonnegative on the latter direction then both 6 and 7 are retained, if nonpositive then 2 is retained, and a zero value retains all three. This is valid even when the mark is in the cap interior. The two direction groups are disjoint and distinct from the own mark. Their score plus the own mark is B+min(G,C).

If C≤G, T partitions as A+G+L+(B+C), each summand at most D. If C>G, T partitions as A+L+(B+G)+C; the third summand is at most D by definition, the fourth by C≤B+G. The equality case C=G is included in the first case. All scores are positive and at most T, so the accepted raw centroid transfer applies at the same mark.
